nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a closed PCF term of ground type $\mathsf{nat}$ and let $n$ be a natural number. If the denotation of $t$ in the empty environment is defined with value $n$, then $t$ evaluates to the numeral $\mathsf{succ}^n(\mathsf{zero})$.
nodes.title: Computational adequacy for PCF

nodes.summary: For every PCF type $A$ and every closed term $t$ of type $A$, the least element $\bot$ of the domain of $A$ formally approximates $t$.
nodes.title: The least element approximates every term

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a PCF term of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, let $\eta$ be a semantic environment for $\Gamma$, and let $\sigma$ assign to each variable of $\Gamma$ a closed term of the same type. Suppose that for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, of type $B$ say, the value of $x$ in $\eta$ formally approximates the closed term $\sigma(x)$ at type $B$. Then the denotation of $t$ in $\eta$ formally approximates, at type…
nodes.title: Fundamental lemma of formal approximation

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a PCF type, let $t$ and $t'$ be closed terms of type $A$, and let $d$ be an element of the domain of $A$. If $t$ evaluates to every closed term $v$ to which $t'$ evaluates, and $d$ formally approximates $t'$, then $d$ formally approximates $t$.
nodes.title: Formal approximation is closed under head expansion

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a PCF type, $t$ a closed term of type $A$ and $(c_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ a chain in the domain of $A$. If every $c_i$ formally approximates $t$, then the supremum $\bigsqcup_i c_i$ formally approximates $t$.
nodes.title: Formal approximation is closed under suprema of chains

nodes.summary: For each PCF type $A$, the relation "$d$ formally approximates $t$" between an element $d$ of the domain of $A$ and a closed term $t$ of type $A$ is defined by recursion on $A$. At the ground type, whose domain is the flat domain of partial natural numbers, $d$ formally approximates $t$ when, for every natural number $n$ such that $d$ is defined with value $n$, the term $t$ evaluates to the numeral $n$. At a…
nodes.title: Formal approximation relation

For PCF one-hole contexts $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$ such that the hole of $C_1$ takes terms of the type and typing context that $C_2$ produces, and the hole of $C_2$ takes terms of the type and typing context that…
nodes.title: Associativity of PCF context composition

The composite $C \circ D$ is the context obtained from $C$ by replacing its hole by $D$; its hole…
nodes.title: Composition of PCF contexts

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $u$ be PCF terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$. If $t$ and $u$ are contextually equivalent, then for every one-hole context $D$ whose hole takes terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$, the terms $D[t]$ and $D[u]$ obtained by plugging $t$ and $u$ into the hole of $D$ are contextually equivalent.
nodes.title: Contextual equivalence in PCF is a congruence

nodes.summary: Given a substitution $\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and a term $a$ of type $A$ in $\Delta$, the extended substitution goes from $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ to $\Delta$: it sends the newest variable to $a$ and every older variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.title: Extending a PCF substitution by a term

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $u$ be PCF terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$, and write $[\![s]\!]$ for the denotation of a term $s$. If $[\![t]\!]\eta \le [\![u]\!]\eta$ in the domain denoted by $A$ for every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, then $t$ contextually approximates $u$.
nodes.title: Denotational approximation implies contextual approximation in PCF

For PCF terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$, $t$ contextually approximates $u$ when, for every one-hole context $C$ whose hole takes terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$ and which produces closed terms of the ground type of natural numbers, and for every natural number $n$: if $C[t]$ evaluates to…
nodes.title: Contextual approximation in PCF

nodes.summary: PCF terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type in the same typing context are contextually equivalent if and only if $t$ contextually approximates $u$ and $u$ contextually approximates $t$.
nodes.title: Contextual equivalence is mutual contextual approximation in PCF

nodes.summary: If two PCF terms $t$ and $u$ of the same type in the same typing context have the same denotation, as continuous maps from environments to the domain of their type, then $t$ and $u$ are contextually equivalent.
nodes.title: Equal denotations imply contextual equivalence in PCF

nodes.summary: Write $C[s]$ for the term obtained by plugging $s$ into the hole of a one-hole context $C$. PCF terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$ are contextually equivalent when, for every one-hole context $C$ whose hole takes terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$ and which produces closed terms of the ground type of natural numbers, and for every natural number $n$, $C[t]$ evaluates to the numeral…
nodes.title: Contextual equivalence in PCF

nodes.summary: Fix a typing context $\Gamma$ and a type $A$. A one-hole context to $(\Delta, B)$ has a hole that takes a term of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$ and turns it into a term of type $B$ in typing context $\Delta$. These contexts are generated by the following rules, for typing contexts $\Delta$, $\Delta'$ and types $B$, $C$, with $\mathbb{N}$ the ground type of natural numbers. The hole itself is a context to…
nodes.title: One-hole contexts of PCF

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a PCF type and let $t$ and $v$ be closed terms of type $A$. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ under big-step call-by-name evaluation, then for every environment $\eta$ of the empty context, the denotations of $t$ and $v$ at $\eta$ are equal.
nodes.title: Soundness of the PCF denotational semantics

nodes.summary: For every PCF term $t$ of type $A \to A$ in a context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$, the denotation of $\mathsf{fix}\,t$ at $\eta$ equals the denotation of the application $t\,(\mathsf{fix}\,t)$ at $\eta$.
nodes.title: Fixed-point equation for the PCF denotation of fix

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a PCF term of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, let $a$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, and let $\eta$ be an environment for $\Gamma$. Writing $[\![s]\!]\eta$ for the denotation of a term $s$ at $\eta$, the denotation at $\eta$ of the term obtained from $t$ by substituting $a$ for the newest variable equals $\![t]\!$, the denotation of $t$ at the…
nodes.title: PCF denotation of instantiation

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a closed PCF term of the ground type of natural numbers and let $n$ be a natural number. If $t$ evaluates to the numeral for $n$, then for every environment $\eta$ of the empty context, the denotation of $t$ at $\eta$ is the defined element $n$ of the flat domain of partial natural numbers.
nodes.title: Closed PCF terms that evaluate to a numeral denote its value

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $u$ be PCF terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$ with the same denotation, and let $C$ be a one-hole context whose hole takes terms of type $A$ in typing context $\Gamma$. Then the terms $C[t]$ and $C[u]$ obtained by plugging $t$ and $u$ into the hole of $C$ have the same denotation.
nodes.title: Equal denotations are preserved by plugging into PCF contexts

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a one-hole context that turns terms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ into terms of type $B$ in context $\Delta$, and let $t$ and $u$ be terms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$. Write $C[s]$ for the term obtained by plugging a term $s$ into the hole of $C$, and $[\![ s ]\!]\,\eta$ for the denotation of a term $s$ in an environment $\eta$, ordered in the domain of its type. If…
nodes.title: Plugging into a PCF context is monotone in the denotation

Then the denotation at $\eta$ of the renaming of $t$ along $\rho$ equals the denotation of $t$ at the environment for $\Gamma$ that gives each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ the value of the variable $\rho(x)$ in…
nodes.title: PCF denotation of a renamed term

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a type-preserving substitution assigning to each variable of a context $\Gamma$ a PCF term in a context $\Delta$, let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, and let $\eta$ be an environment for $\Delta$. Then the denotation at $\eta$ of the term obtained by applying $\sigma$ to $t$ equals the denotation of $t$ at the environment for $\Gamma$ that gives each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ the value…
nodes.title: PCF denotation of a substituted term

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a PCF term of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, let $\eta$ be an environment for $\Gamma$, and let $b$ be an element of the domain of a type $B$. The denotation of the weakening of $t$ (the same term in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $B$) at the extended environment $(\eta, b)$ equals the denotation of $t$ at $\eta$.
nodes.title: Weakening preserves the PCF denotation

nodes.summary: The denotation of a PCF term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is the Scott-continuous map $[\![t]\!]$ from environments for $\Gamma$ to the domain of $A$, defined by recursion on $t$: a variable denotes its lookup map; $[\![\lambda t]\!]$ is the currying of $[\![t]\!]$; $[\![f\,a]\!]\eta = [\![f]\!]\eta\,([\![a]\!]\eta)$; $[\![\mathsf{zero}]\!]$ is constantly the defined value $0$;…
nodes.title: Denotation of PCF terms

nodes.summary: One-step call-by-name reduction of closed PCF terms is deterministic: if a closed term $t$ of type $A$ reduces in one step to $t_1$ and also reduces in one step to $t_2$, then $t_1 = t_2$.
nodes.title: Determinism of PCF call-by-name reduction

nodes.summary: For closed PCF terms $t$, $v$, $w$ of the same type, if $t \Downarrow v$ and $t \Downarrow w$ under big-step call-by-name evaluation, then $v = w$.
nodes.title: Determinism of PCF big-step evaluation

nodes.summary: The ω-complete partial order denoted by a PCF type is defined by recursion on the type: the ground type denotes the flat domain of partial natural numbers, and a function type $A \to B$ denotes the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps from the domain of $A$ to the domain of $B$.
nodes.title: Domain of a PCF type

nodes.summary: The ω-complete partial order of environments for a context $\Gamma$ (a list of PCF types) is defined by recursion on $\Gamma$: the empty context has the one-point order, and the environments for $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ are the pairs $(\eta, a)$ of an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ and an element $a$ of the domain of $A$, ordered componentwise.
nodes.title: Semantic environments for PCF

nodes.summary: If a closed PCF term $v$ of the ground type of natural numbers is a value, then $v$ is the numeral $\mathsf{succ}^n\,\mathsf{zero}$ for some natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Closed values of ground type are numerals

nodes.summary: Let $t$, $t'$ and $v$ be closed PCF terms of type $A$. If $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one call-by-name step and $t'$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-name semantics, then $t$ evaluates to $v$.
nodes.title: Backward reduction preserves evaluation in PCF

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $v$ be closed PCF terms of type $A$. If $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) call-by-name steps and $v$ is a value, then $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-name semantics.
nodes.title: Reduction to a value implies big-step evaluation in PCF

nodes.summary: For closed PCF terms $t$ and $v$ of type $A$, $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-name semantics if and only if $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) call-by-name steps and $v$ is a value.
nodes.title: Big-step evaluation agrees with small-step reduction in PCF

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, a closed PCF term $t$ of ground type evaluates to the numeral $n$ if and only if the denotation of $t$ is the defined value $n$.
nodes.title: Evaluation to a numeral agrees with the denotation

nodes.summary: Write $\underline{n}$ for the numeral $\mathsf{succ}^n\,\mathsf{zero}$. For closed PCF terms $t$ and $v$ of the same type, $t \Downarrow v$ ($t$ evaluates to $v$) is the least relation closed under the following rules, where all terms are closed and $n$ ranges over natural numbers. Every $\lambda$-abstraction evaluates to itself, and $\mathsf{zero} \Downarrow \mathsf{zero}$. If $t \Downarrow \underline{n}$, then…
nodes.title: Big-step call-by-name evaluation of PCF

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$, the identity substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma$ sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting of $x$ alone.
nodes.title: Identity PCF substitution

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an ω-complete partial order and let $t$, $s_1$, $s_2$ be Scott-continuous maps from $\alpha$ to the flat domain of partial natural numbers. Their strict zero test is the Scott-continuous map sending $x \in \alpha$ to $s_1(x)$ if $t(x)$ is defined and equal to $0$, to $s_2(x)$ if $t(x)$ is defined and nonzero, and to the undefined value if $t(x)$ is undefined.
nodes.title: Strict zero test as a continuous map

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, let $b$ be a term of type $B$ in $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and let $a$ be a term of type $A$ in $\Delta$. Applying the lift of $\sigma$ to $b$ and then instantiating the newest variable with $a$ gives the same term as applying to $b$ the extension of $\sigma$ by $a$, which sends the newest variable to $a$ and…
nodes.title: Instantiation after substitution under a binder

nodes.summary: Given a term $b$ of type $B$ in a context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and a term $a$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the instantiation of $b$ with $a$ is the term of type $B$ in $\Gamma$ obtained by applying to $b$ the substitution that sends the newest variable to $a$ and every older variable to itself.
nodes.title: Instantiating the newest variable of a PCF term

nodes.summary: Given a substitution $\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and a type $A$, the lift of $\sigma$ is the substitution from $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ to $\Delta$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ that sends the newest variable to the newest variable and every older variable $x$ to the weakening of $\sigma(x)$ by one variable.
nodes.title: Lifting a PCF substitution under a binder

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, the lookup of $x$ is the Scott-continuous map from environments for $\Gamma$ to the domain of $A$ defined by recursion on $x$: if $x$ is the newest variable, it sends an environment $(\eta, a)$ to $a$; if $x$ is the shift of a variable $y$ of the older context, it sends $(\eta, a)$ to the lookup of $y$ at $\eta$.
nodes.title: Variable lookup in a PCF environment

nodes.summary: The ground type $\mathsf{nat}$ of natural numbers is the unique base type of PCF, whose types are the simple types over a single base type.
nodes.title: Natural number type of PCF

nodes.summary: If $v$ is a closed PCF value of type $A$ (an abstraction or a numeral), then there is no closed term $t'$ such that $v$ reduces to $t'$ in one call-by-name step.
nodes.title: PCF values are normal forms

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$ and natural number $n$, the numeral of $n$ is the term $\mathsf{succ}^n(\mathsf{zero})$ of type $\mathsf{nat}$ in $\Gamma$: the numeral of $0$ is $\mathsf{zero}$, and the numeral of $n + 1$ is $\mathsf{succ}$ applied to the numeral of $n$.
nodes.title: PCF numerals

nodes.summary: In every context, the map sending a natural number $n$ to the numeral $\mathsf{succ}^n(\mathsf{zero})$ of type $\mathsf{nat}$ is injective: distinct natural numbers give distinct numerals.
nodes.title: Injectivity of PCF numerals

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the closed numeral $\mathrm{succ}^n\,\mathrm{zero}$ of type nat does not reduce: there is no closed term $t'$ such that $\mathrm{succ}^n\,\mathrm{zero}$ reduces to $t'$ in one call-by-name step.
nodes.title: PCF numerals are normal forms

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the closed PCF numeral $\underline{n} = \mathsf{succ}^n\,\mathsf{zero}$ evaluates to itself under big-step call-by-name evaluation: $\underline{n} \Downarrow \underline{n}$.
nodes.title: Numerals evaluate to themselves

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a context, that is, a list of PCF types, and suppose that for every type $A$ and every variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ we are given a value $f(x)$ in the domain denoted by $A$. The environment built from $f$ is the environment for $\Gamma$ defined by recursion on $\Gamma$: for the empty context it is the unique element of the one-point domain, and for the context obtained from $\Gamma'$ by…
nodes.title: Environment from a family of values

nodes.summary: For every type $A$ and every closed PCF term $v$ of type $A$ that is a value, $v \Downarrow v$ under big-step call-by-name evaluation.
nodes.title: PCF values evaluate to themselves

nodes.summary: For every PCF type $A$, the domain denoted by $A$ has a least element, defined by recursion on $A$: at the ground type it is the undefined element of the flat domain of partial natural numbers, and at a function type $B \to C$ it is the continuous map that sends every argument to the least element of the domain denoted by $C$.
nodes.title: Least elements of PCF domains

Write $K[t]$ for the term obtained by plugging a term $t$ into the hole of a context $K$, and $D \circ E$ for the context obtained by replacing the hole of $D$ by $E$. Then…

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a one-hole context that turns terms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ into terms of type $B$ in context $\Delta$, and $t$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$. The term $C[t]$ of type $B$ in context $\Delta$ is defined by recursion on $C$: if $C$ is the hole, $C[t] = t$; if $C$ applies a term former (abstraction, application on either side, successor, predecessor, the zero test at any of its three…
nodes.title: Plugging a term into a PCF context

nodes.summary: Every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ contextually approximates itself.
nodes.title: Contextual approximation in PCF is reflexive

nodes.summary: Every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is contextually equivalent to itself.
nodes.title: Contextual equivalence in PCF is reflexive

nodes.summary: For contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ (lists of PCF types), a renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ is a map sending each variable of $\Gamma$ of type $A$, for every type $A$, to a variable of $\Delta$ of the same type $A$; it is the STLC notion of renaming at PCF types.
nodes.title: PCF renamings

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$, type $A$ and term $t$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, renaming $t$ along the identity renaming of $\Gamma$ gives $t$.
nodes.title: Renaming a PCF term by the identity

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and $\rho$ a renaming from $\Delta$ to a context $\Xi$. For every PCF term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, renaming along $\rho$ the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$ gives the result of applying to $t$ the substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the renaming of $\sigma(x)$ along $\rho$.
nodes.title: Renaming after substitution in PCF

nodes.summary: Given a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the renaming along $\rho$ of a PCF term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is the term of type $A$ in context $\Delta$ obtained by replacing each variable $x$ by $\rho(x)$. Under a $\lambda$-binder, $\rho$ is replaced by its lift, which sends the bound variable to itself and the successor of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the successor of…
nodes.title: Renaming of PCF terms

nodes.summary: For a PCF term $a$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$, this is the substitution from the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ to $\Gamma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable $x$ to the variable $x$ of $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Single-variable substitution in PCF

nodes.summary: Write $\underline{n}$ for the numeral $\mathrm{succ}^n\,\mathrm{zero}$, and $b[a]$ for the result of substituting the closed term $a$ for the bound variable of an abstraction body $b$. One-step call-by-name reduction $t \to t'$ between closed PCF terms of the same type is the least relation closed under these rules: $f\,a \to f'\,a$ whenever $f \to f'$; $(\lambda b)\,a \to b[a]$, without evaluating $a$;…
nodes.title: Call-by-name reduction step of PCF

nodes.summary: Let $t$ and $v$ be closed PCF terms of type $A$. If $t$ evaluates to $v$ in the big-step call-by-name semantics, then $t$ reduces to $v$ in finitely many (possibly zero) call-by-name steps.
nodes.title: Big-step evaluation implies reduction in PCF

nodes.summary: For closed PCF terms $t$ and $t'$ of the same type, $t \to^* t'$ holds when $t$ reduces to $t'$ in finitely many, possibly zero, one-step call-by-name reductions; that is, $\to^*$ is the reflexive transitive closure of one-step reduction.
nodes.title: Multi-step call-by-name reduction of PCF

nodes.summary: A substitution from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ (lists of PCF types) assigns to every variable of $\Gamma$, of any type $A$, a PCF term of type $A$ in context $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Parallel substitutions for PCF

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a renaming from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and $\sigma$ a substitution from $\Delta$ to a context $\Xi$. For every PCF term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, applying $\sigma$ to the renaming of $t$ along $\rho$ gives the result of applying to $t$ the substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(\rho(x))$.
nodes.title: Substitution after renaming in PCF

nodes.title: Composition of PCF substitutions

nodes.title: Substitution in PCF terms

nodes.summary: A closed PCF term $t$ of ground type evaluates to some term if and only if its denotation, an element of the flat domain of partial natural numbers, is defined.
nodes.title: Termination agrees with definedness of the denotation

nodes.summary: Write $\mathsf{nat}$ for the ground type of natural numbers and $A \Rightarrow B$ for the type of functions from $A$ to $B$. The intrinsically typed PCF terms of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ (a list of PCF types) are generated by the following rules: every variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ is a term of type $A$; if $t$ has type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, then $\lambda t$…
nodes.title: PCF terms

nodes.summary: PCF types are the simple types over a single ground type, the type of natural numbers.
nodes.title: PCF types

nodes.summary: For closed PCF terms $t$ and $v$ of the same type, if $t \Downarrow v$ under big-step call-by-name evaluation, then $v$ is a value.
nodes.title: PCF evaluation results are values

nodes.summary: A closed PCF term is a value when it is a $\lambda$-abstraction or the numeral $\mathsf{succ}^n\,\mathsf{zero}$ for some natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Values of PCF

nodes.summary: PCF uses the typed de Bruijn variables of the simply typed $\lambda$-calculus over a single base type: a variable of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ is a position in the list $\Gamma$ at which $A$ occurs.
nodes.title: PCF variables

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a context and $A$, $B$ types. Weakening sends a PCF term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ to the term of type $A$ in the context obtained by prepending a new variable of type $B$ to $\Gamma$, by renaming every free variable of $t$ to its successor, that is, by shifting each de Bruijn index up by one.
nodes.title: Weakening of PCF terms

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
